extracted.intended_audience: children's book illustrators, librarians, publishers, and general readers interested in literary awards
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility, judging rules, and evaluative criteria for the Carnegie Medal for Illustration (formerly the Kate Greenaway Medal), the UK award recognising distinguished illustration in books for children and young people. Covers publication/eligibility rules, CILIP's aesthetic guidance (style, format, visual experience, synergy with text), and the nomination/judging process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timeframe / eligibility year
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated books must be first published in the U.K. during the preceding school year (September to August).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the eligibility window for nominated works. Note: the article also explains that from 2007 the Medal is dated by its presentation year (the year following publication), which affects how years are recorded but not the publication eligibility window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: English must be the language of any text, or one of dual languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a book contains text, English should be used (or appear as one of a dual-language edition) for it to meet the award's stated language criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended readership / target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be published for young people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only books published for children and young people are eligible; the award is specifically for illustration in books aimed at that audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: UK publication / co-publication rule
rubrics_metrics.description: They must be published in the U.K. originally or within three months in case of co-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-publications are allowed provided the UK publication occurs within three months of the other edition. This affects eligibility for books simultaneously issued in other territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusiveness of categories
rubrics_metrics.description: "All categories of illustrated books for children and young people are eligible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award explicitly includes picture books, information/reference books, nonfiction, adaptations/editions, and other illustrated formats; the article gives examples (reference and nonfiction winners) to show the scope is broad within children's/YA illustrated works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic style, format and visual experience
rubrics_metrics.description: CILIP specifies numerous points of artistic style, format, and visual experience that should be considered when judging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are instructed to consider style and format as part of the evaluation; the article summarizes CILIP's guidance but does not reproduce a complete checklist, indicating multiple stylistic/formatting factors inform decisions (examples through winners illustrate diverse approaches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy of illustration and text
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular attention should be paid to the "synergy of illustration and text" where text exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CILIP's guidance emphasises how illustrations and text interact: judges should evaluate how illustrations complement, enhance, or interplay with the written elements rather than treating them in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of graphic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Illustrated work needs to be considered primarily in terms of its graphic elements."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing entries, the visual/graphic qualities of the work are the primary focus; text is secondary except insofar as it interacts with and is enhanced by the imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall visual impact / lasting impression
rubrics_metrics.description: "The whole work should provide pleasure from a stimulating and satisfying visual experience which leaves a lasting impression."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges should consider the book's capacity to give pleasure and to create a memorable visual experience—i.e., lasting emotional or aesthetic impact is a key evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and judging process
rubrics_metrics.description: Library and information professionals in CILIP nominate books in September and October. A panel of 12 children's librarians in CILIP's youth interest group judges books for both the Writing and Illustration awards. The shortlist is announced in March and the winner in June.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rubric describes who may nominate (CILIP professionals), the judging body (12 children's librarians), and the timetable (nominations in Sept–Oct, shortlist in March, winner in June). It implies that selection reflects professional librarians' judgments and follows a set calendar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award/prize components
rubrics_metrics.description: The award by CILIP is a gold Medal and £500 worth of books donated to the illustrator's chosen library. Since 2000 there is also a £5000 cash prize from a bequest by Colin Mears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an evaluative criterion, this describes what the winner receives and is part of the award's rules and rewards structure; the presence of a monetary bequest (since 2000) is noted.
